reports.name: AAFC Outlook for Principal Field Crops (Canada)

outlook: Grains stayed lower through Monday's midday trade. December corn was down 6 cents near $4.68 as warm, dry weather is expected to speed a harvest running behind average, and funds sold more than 85,000 corn contracts in the week to October 13. November soybeans were down about 7 cents near $12.54 even after USDA confirmed sales of 114,000 tonnes to China and 261,000 tonnes to unknown destinations, while Brazil's Mato Grosso passed 50% soybean planting. Minneapolis December spring wheat was down 4 cents near $6.72 and Chicago December wheat down 4 cents near $6.56, pressured by a report that Russia's Putin proposed a U.S.-China-Russia summit on ending the Ukraine war and by Russia seeking Chinese approval to export more wheat; ICE canola remains under C$800 per tonne on Prairie harvest selling.
